items.title: Independence of the Gysin-at-infinity class from the choice of the proper model, up to the induced morphism at infinity
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)

items.difficulty_reason: Extending the Gysin-at-infinity lemma, the statement says that for a proper morphism g : W' -> W which is an isomorphism over A^1_X, the classes C' in A^0(W'_infinity -> X) and C in A^0(W_infinity -> X) constructed there satisfy g_{infinity,*} o C' = C (statement lines 10107-10114). The proof sets b' = b o g, writes i'_infinity for the inclusion of W'_infinity, and compares the two constructions on a single cycle class: for alpha in CH_k(X) one chooses beta' in CH_{k+1}(W') restricting to the flat pullback of alpha on (b')^{-1}A^1_X, observes that its pushforward beta = g_*beta' restricts to the flat pullback of alpha on b^{-1}A^1_X, so beta is an admissible choice in the definition of C, and then invokes the compatibility of the Gysin map with the proper pushforward to get i_infinity^* beta = g_{infinity,*}(i'_infinity)^* beta' (proof lines 10116-10125). Since this holds after any base change by X' -> X locally of finite type, the two classes agree (proof lines 10126-10128). Choosing beta as a pushforward so that both constructions compute the same value is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
